prerequisites: Basic notions from first year courses of Mathematics and Physics.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the main concepts of Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer.
I and II Law of Thermodynamics for closed and open systems.
Models of state thermodynamics.
Applications of I and II Thermodynamics Law on components of heating systems.
Properties and transformations of the moist air.
Steam power plant.
Heat pump and refrigeration system.
Conduction heat transfer.
Convection heat transfer.
Radiative heat transfer.
Finned systems.
Calculate the thermodynamic properties.
Analyze the components of a heating system in terms of I and II law.
Analyze a thermal power plant in terms of I and II law.
Analyze in terms of I and II law heat pumps / refrigeration systems.
Translate heat transfer problems into formal language.
Address the corresponding analytical solution, even approximately or graphically.
Knowing how to select the most appropriate methodologies to address the study involving energy transformations and to heat transfer.
Ability to represent, by written and oral tests, the concepts acquired during the course in a clear and concise way and with an appropriate technical language.
Ability to use and apply in several contexts the habits acquired so to deepen technical problems.

syllabus_topics: First law of thermodynamics for closed systems
First law of thermodynamics for isolated systems
Other formulations of the first law of thermodynamics for a closed system
Limits of the first law of thermodynamics
Second law of thermodynamics for closed systems
Second law of thermodynamics for isolated systems
Second law of thermodynamics for closed systems
I and II law of thermodynamics (for open systems)
Liquids, solids, steam and gas: models, calculation of the properties and transformations
Property, equations of state, psychrometric chart, elementary transformations
Steam operator plant: refrigerator and heat pump
The relation of heat transfer to thermodynamics
Constitutive and balance equations for heat transfer
Steady one-dimensional heat conduction in simple geometries for homogeneous and inhomogeneous problems
Analytical solutions for the slab, Heisler charts
Dimensionless boundary layer equations and similarity parameters
Procedures for evaluating the convection heat transfer coefficient
Bulk temperature and heat transfer coefficient for internal convection
The simplifications of the fully developed regions
Thermal radiation: spectral and directional features
Intensity of the radiation for calculating the radiative heat fluxes
Radiative characteristics of opaque surfaces: emission - absorption - reflection, definitions and models
Relationship between the emission, absorption and reflection
Heat transfer between diffuse gray surfaces
assessment_rules: Students must pass written tests with a minimum rating of 18/30 to access the oral exams. The final grade is the average of the results achieved in the Applied Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer parts. Honors are attributed for high-level theoretical and operative skills, good communication, and autonomous processing capabilities.
